html:
Colchis was an ancient land and kingdom on the eastern coast of the Black Sea, in what is now western Georgia. Its people, the Colchians, were probably ancestors of today's Laz and Mingrelians. It is shown here in 323 and 300 BCE.

To the Greeks it was the edge of the known world and the home of the Golden Fleece, which Jason and the Argonauts sailed to steal. The legend may echo real wealth: Colchis was known for gold, worked iron, linen and timber. From the 6th century BCE Greek traders founded colonies on its coast, such as Phasis and Dioscurias.

Colchis was loosely tied to the Persian Empire and later dealt with its neighbour, the Georgian kingdom of Iberia, to the east. In the early 1st century BCE it fell to Mithridates VI of Pontus, and after his defeat it came under Roman influence. The later kingdom of Lazica grew from it.
